scope: General compiler loop-invariant motion, monotonic rejection exits, and reciprocal reuse for proven invariant divisors. No interpreter changes or runtime cache.

method.device: ESP32 rev3.1, 240MHz, one core, standalone profiling image, Wi-Fi off, GPIO untouched. Same prepared workloads, parameters and 32 timestamps per case as the accepted baseline. CRC and serial output outside timed evaluation.
method.hotspots: Interrupted PCs at 997 and 1999 microseconds, bracketed by two unsampled controls. Self-symbol percentages include inlined helpers. Estimated time is sample share times the unsampled warm mean, not separately timed functions.
method.host: Preparation, output-equivalence checks and separately instrumented instruction counts only. No new laptop timing comparison.
method.equivalence: All 608 host frame CRCs, active-effect counts, pixel counts and timestamps match the baseline. All 544 device frames verified against the host manifest; all 17 cases completed and all 16 profiling/control windows captured.
method.limitations: Prepared evaluation and output-buffer encoding only. No network, storage, DMA or physical LED latency is included. A 32-frame window does not establish whole-show worst-case deadlines.

artifacts.final_compiler_reproduction: After a lint-only iterator cleanup, the final compiler reproduced all 19 prepared archives and their manifest byte-for-byte.

division_count_scope: Executed FloatDivide plus FloatDivideIntoConst bytecode only. Does not count divisions inside other instructions, source evaluation, context construction, or color helpers.
memory_notes: All other measured retained sizes unchanged. All evaluation allocation counts zero. Retained deltas include bytecode and ordinary scalar registers; no cache was added.
interpretation: Stanford mean evaluation time falls 30.74 percent; FreezeFrame-over-black falls 45.43 percent. Both source sample counts are unchanged.
Chase/Pulse also improves, showing reciprocal reuse is not tied to the temporal operator or even to loops.
Unchanged Shimmer bytecode and nearly unchanged warm time are a control; its small cold-window difference is not attributed to the compiler passes.
The starter port's one-microsecond mean increase is not meaningful against its first-frame cost and lower warm controls. No material regression was observed in this workload set.
Stanford remains over the 60Hz evaluation budget for all sampled frames. FreezeFrame-over-black fits 60Hz but exceeds the 120Hz budget on all sampled frames.
Software division's sample percentage rises as total time falls. Its estimated absolute cost decreases; remaining division includes work outside division bytecode.

full_firmware.build: dig-quad loader with Wi-Fi, storage and I2S

validation.focused_optimization_tests: 12 passed, including 7 added for these passes
